requirements.text: Develop the strategic plan through fact-finding, future vision, scenario development and plan preparation, integrating existing service-line, behavioral-health and telehealth plans.
Assess current and future market and organizational position, including demographics, payer mix, inpatient/outpatient/surgical market share, industry trends and system leakage.
Conduct a system-of-care survey and 20-30 interviews to assess service-line offerings and performance and complement quantitative analysis.
Analyze policy, reimbursement, technology and care-delivery trends and identify growth opportunities aligned with UNMH clinical, research and fiscal priorities.
Define implementation goals, tactics and required resources, including consideration of value-based revenue, strategic financial models and facility-investment priorities.
Project inpatient and outpatient volumes over three-, five- and ten-year horizons using market analysis and leadership input, with adjustments for COVID-19 effects.
Document facility deficiencies affecting operations or patient satisfaction and analyze alternative strategies for future inpatient and outpatient service and facility needs.
Analyze outpatient referral and utilization patterns and model how alternative growth strategies affect inpatient services.
Assess opportunities to consolidate or expand selected services with other healthcare providers.
Recommend how emerging technologies affect building design and IT infrastructure and assess IT opportunities for greater health-system integration.
Work with the strategic planning committee and key stakeholders on findings and recommendations and support requested trustee or stakeholder presentations.

exclusions: Historical solicitation issued September 2, 2020 with a September 14, 2020 deadline; no present opening or current timetable is asserted.
Private strategic plans, referral and utilization records, financial data, facility evidence and stakeholder availability are missing; no invented forecasts or interview findings.
No clinical decisions, patient care, negotiations, construction, approvals or implementation are authorized by this normalization.
Additional consulting is contingent on later requests; do not assume a fixed subsequent workload or resolved contract duration.

projects.buyer: City of Duluth, City Attorney’s Office
projects.title: City Attorney’s Office Case Management Software Solution
projects.summary: Historical 2020 RFP to replace the City Attorney’s case-management system with software, necessary hardware, implementation, training and support for approximately 20 named users. Scope spans criminal and civil cases, documents, contracts, claims, reporting, integrations and migration.

requirements.text: Provide the replacement platform and deployment/support specifications for about 20 named users; address on-premise VMware and Windows/SQL Server 2016-or-newer compatibility and CJIS encryption capabilities, with web-based deployment preferred.
Provide Laserfiche and Microsoft Office/Outlook interfaces and Minnesota Courts networking specifications; assess Active Directory and Citrix compatibility.
Convert criminal case data from TCP3 and assess any necessary conversion of internally maintained civil-case data.
Manage case contacts, documents, notes, tasks, email and calendar events with user-specific security and access.
Support prioritized task scheduling, assignments, alerts and progress tracking for projects and files.

Provide criminal/civil document search, retention and MNCIS/BCA/AXON interfaces; tracked e-discovery, original-preserving redaction/versioning, Bates numbering, OCR and batch document generation; victim/witness separation, diversion/specialty-court tracking, configurable file numbering, private notes, flexible case searches and reduced duplicate entry.
Track contract expirations and renewals with calendar/task reminders and customizable contract reporting.
Track claims with financial reporting and transfer claim files to litigation when lawsuits are filed.
Generate criminal, civil, claims and customized reports, including MNCIS financial updates for restitution/fines, pending cases and VOCA PMT victim-grant reporting.
Link email to files and synchronize tasks, calendars and MNCIS court dates with Outlook.

Support mobile/remote and requested offline editing (connectivity requirements unresolved), multiple browser sessions, configurable required fields, validation, restricted fields, duplicate alerts/merging and single-editor record locking.
Provide initial role-specific training, documentation, regular software updates, a formal upgrade/issue process and business-hours technical support.

exclusions: Historical solicitation issued September 8, 2020 with proposals due October 1, 2020; no current opportunity is asserted.
No access to criminal/civil files, TCP3 exports, legal records, evidence systems, court interfaces or production credentials; integrations and migrations require authorization.
The preferred Laserfiche direction is case-system to Laserfiche, not a mandatory direction. Civil migration is conditional; web-based deployment is preferred rather than universally mandatory.
No legal advice, case decisions, evidence alteration or production implementation is authorized by this draft.

projects.title: Information Systems Risk Assessment for the Integrity Data Hub
projects.summary: Historical 2020 RFP for independent assessment of the Integrity Data Hub, its security plan, operations, controls and IDH-controlled AWS environment, with recurring security reviews and penetration testing. An HTTPS Wayback capture is byte-identical to the requested HTTP PDF; conflicting dates and assessment counts remain unresolved.

requirements.text: Prepare a System Security Assessment Plan based on the existing SSP, covering all 18 control groups initially and a proposed subsequent three-year rolling review cycle, using the existing Q1 2020 penetration test for the initial assessment.
Independently assess IDH security and data-protection controls, operations and the IDH-controlled hosted environment against its Moderate classification and applicable NIST/FISMA/OMB requirements.
Review and benchmark security policies and practices, discuss gaps with management and develop revised policies and standards.

Perform authorized external vulnerability testing, black-box/grey-box penetration testing, management-coordinated social-engineering checks and review of AWS physical-access provisions without compromising system or data operations.
Report testing scenarios, findings and severity/risk scores and recommend remediations and corrective-action or milestone plans.
Evaluate malware-protection software, systems and procedures and analyze related threats and weaknesses.
Evaluate logon methods and policies for staff, administrators, developers and external users and recommend improvements.

Assess NIST-CSF cybersecurity maturity across governance, people, risk management, operations and continuity; rate and prioritize gaps, compare peers, propose mitigation timelines and recommend ongoing annual progress reviews.
Deliver the final risk and SSP assessment with prioritized improvements, an executive summary and a presentation suitable for non-technical management.

exclusions: This historical RFP is not testing authorization. No penetration tests, social engineering, production access or changes may be performed without explicit authorization and rules of engagement.
The private SSP, system configurations, prior test results, controls evidence and claims data are unavailable; no security findings are inferred from the public RFP.
Assessment data must follow the source controls for encryption, US-based cloud storage, restricted sharing and post-analysis purging.
Do not choose a definitive proposal deadline or assessment count from conflicting source passages; no current procurement is asserted.

projects.title: Hemisfair Augmented Reality Project: Tree Donor Recognition
projects.summary: Historical June 2021 RFP for a Hemisfair-owned augmented-reality tree-donor app with a $50,000-$100,000 budget range and approximately 230 trees in Yanaguana Garden and Civic Park. The requested pilot launch was December 1, 2021, with Civic Park rollout in 2023.

requirements.text: Develop a Hemisfair-branded, Hemisfair-owned AR app for iOS and Android targeting all iPhone, iPad and Android models as requested and covering the two named parks.
Use QR codes and GPS to activate the experience; provide entrance/tree codes, custom badge design and the first 250 physical QR badges for HPARC staff to install.
Show donor-recognition photos, text and optional recorded tributes near claimed trees; route unclaimed-tree scans to tree-planting program information.
Provide recognition-name search, interactive tree maps and walking directions, program information, donation links and sponsor recognition.
Meet the requested ADA digital-accessibility standards, including captions, distinguishable controls and minimal flashing; consider Spanish translation where feasible.
Provide an easy-to-learn staff content-management system for tree donor records, define photo/audio/text parameters and provide a way to acquire additional QR badges.
Train two HPARC staff members to maintain the system.
Prepare a proposed AR-app FAQ for publication on Hemisfair’s website.
Provide a one-year service and support warranty.

exclusions: Historic July 2, 2021 proposal deadline and 2021/2023 rollout dates are not current commitments.

QR badge installation is assigned to HPARC staff, not the vendor. Tower Park and additions for future phases, historic structures or amenities are potential future scope, not guaranteed baseline work.
Spanish translation is conditional. The all-model device wording is retained as a requested target, not proof of feasible or tested support.

Brand assets, donor media/permissions, CMS accounts and release credentials are unavailable. No physical work, deployment, donor publication or procurement is authorized; FAQ output would be a proposed draft only.

projects.buyer: Efficiency Forward, Inc. DBA DesignLights Consortium
projects.title: Website Design and Development and Web Content Management Solution
projects.summary: Historical May 2020 RFP for an audience-focused DLC website redesign and WCMS, with planning, development, migration, testing and support. Expected launch was six to nine months after contract award. QPL and application-management functionality is excluded from change, while visual integration remains in scope.

requirements.text: Use DLC stakeholder surveys and Cadmus research to confirm audience needs and design goals; review content/structure and recommend CMS, hosting and page/template requirements.

Prepare proposed audience-centered designs with modern navigation, homepage, graphic templates, icons, typography and SEO, preserving clear routes to products, technical requirements and application guidance.
Implement staff-editable WCMS templates and integrate the member portal and consistent QPL/AMS visual presentation without changing QPL or AMS functionality.

Provide non-product website search, organized/dynamic news, searchable blog content, social sharing and audience-engagement options, with website-activity analytics support including Google Analytics.
Provide responsive layouts and WCMS mobile previews/customization, and perform UX testing on all design elements.
Import applicable existing website content into the new site and perform the migration analysis, scripting, testing and coordination needed for that transition.
Provide encrypted system access over HTTPS and obtain service-level commitments from the WCMS OEM rather than only an implementation partner.
Provide staff training and detailed functionality documentation, plus support for questions and timely bug resolution during 9 a.m.-5 p.m. Eastern time.

exclusions: Historical May 6, 2020 release and May 26, 2020 response deadline; the six-to-nine-month launch expectation is relative to the historical award, not a new commitment.

Do not change QPL or AMS functionality; their appearance and integration remain in scope. Dashboards, tutorials and member communication tools are potential sub-projects, not unconditional baseline commitments.
DLC/Cadmus research, source content exports, member-portal data, analytics access and production credentials are unavailable. No migration, deployment or private-system access is authorized.
Capability questions about 24/7 service, hosting models and optional integrations are not treated as promises or mandatory delivered features; no budget or fixed deployment model is invented.
